hed: A Quiet Morning on the Desk
deck: Table Rock this morning: 911.44 ft. Taneycomo still eats on a pink worm if the generators give you a window.

play.title: Fish the wind.
play.body: Fall bass set up where the shad get blown. A crankbait that bangs is better than a worm that sits.

season.name: Fall turnover
season.why: The lake turns over and the fish don't read the same book they did in August. Crankbaits get good again. Trout streamers get good. This is the season Branson locals wait for.
tips: Windblown banks and shad-colored cranks, 8–18 feet.
Walleye on the same gravel they used all summer, just shallower.
Taneycomo: streamers and wooly buggers when they generate. Hoppers until the first frost.
A jacket in the boat. Dawn is cold before the strip is.

tomorrow: Tomorrow we print a new level, a new play, and whether the dam spun overnight. Open it before you drive. The water will have moved.
weekGraf: The pool walked down from 911.68 early in the week to 911.44 this morning — about 0.24 ft off that earlier mark, still under the 915 full pool. 5 mornings this week the desk had no new gage (carry-forward). Numbers marked “desk” were read from that day’s scout; “carry” was not. Ramps are still in. Shallow coves feel a falling pool first.

now.temp: Verify at the ramp — scout does not invent dawn temps
now.clarity: Clear near the dam; arms can stain. Verify locally.

body: With the lake about 3.56 feet down, it's showing more bank than usual. Stumps and other hazards sit closer to the surface in the shallow coves, creek arms and near some ramps. Take it slow up the James, Kings and Long Creek arms, and expect a longer walk at a few launches.

The surface has cooled into the low- to mid-70s with excellent clarity. Bass have been hitting topwaters and soft plastics early. As the sun climbs, they move to jigs, live bait and drop-shot rigs around long points and gravel flats that drop into 20 to 40 feet, and onto offshore structure. Some mornings have produced solid numbers. The mixed bag is there too — walleye are holding on points in 20 to 25 feet, and crappie and spotted bass keep coming out of the deeper brush and around the docks.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad. Do not guess the generators.

body: The trout water runs cold all year because it's fed by releases from the bottom of Table Rock, and steady stocking keeps it full of rainbows and improving numbers of browns. On this water, generation decides how you fish. When the dam is quiet overnight and early, you can wade, drift light line or fish an indicator. When the current builds, usually from afternoon into evening, you want weight on the line and a drift that works the seams and the structure.

From the dam down to Fall Creek is trophy water. It's artificial lures and flies only, and every rainbow between 12 and 20 inches goes back. Wade it during the low windows, outside the closed zone, with micro jigs and small flies. Save the pink worms under a float, the mega and San Juan worms and the egg patterns for the water below Fall Creek. Anyone keeping trout needs a trout permit. On moving water, drift boats and dock anglers do best by staying in the current breaks with heavier setups. Recent reports like Lilleys' (Oct 1) and John Sappington (early Oct) highlight marabou jigs in black, sculpin and olive (Indy orange head favorite), zebra midges in red and black, scuds, and night fishing with streamers or small jerkbaits. In water this clear, clean and natural wins, and a black jig after dark is still hard to beat. Call SWPA at 866-494-1993 before you head out.

editor.note: Two-lake daily rebuilt from the morning fishing scout plus the prior week of files. We print a level only when the scout had one. Carry-forward mornings are labeled. No invented bite ratings. Call 866-494-1993 before wading Taneycomo.
